current_backend_fact: stages_mixed validates all materials as MCC and calls mcc_split with typed MCC history; MC is explicitly unsupported
hypothesis_not_a_diagnosis: Volume-preserving plastic flow can make displacement elements too restrictive. The current displacement discrepancy alone does not prove locking or identify its cause.

primary_sources.title: Yang, Song, Chen (2000), Volumetric locking analysis and element choice in3D elastoplastic analysis of soil, Engineering Mechanics17(6),6-13
primary_sources.verified_scope: Publisher abstract analyses locking for MC soil and particular brick/enhanced elements; it does not validate our Tet10 discretization.

primary_sources.title: Finite element response sensitivity analysis using three-field mixed formulation: General theory and application to frame structures
primary_sources.verified_scope: Indexed primary abstract discusses history-dependent constitutive stress in three-field weak equations; page returned robot verification, so no full text or implementation detail claimed.

staged_implementation_and_required_evide: Typed split material response: independent deviatoric engineering strain and volume; preserve original MC parameters and all MC state variants; never disguise MC as an MCC state.
Retain the existing MCC implicit update byte exactly, dispatch MC to its existing fixed-partition primal and nonsymmetric tangent; no symmetrization, bulk clipping or changed flow/dilation.

Before global wiring: independently verify elastic bulk/shear responses including near incompressibility, MC face/edges/Rankine/apex, arbitrary rotations and history, split directional Jacobians and stress work; real no-solution input must remain a failure with no history mutation.

Introduce an explicitly identified MC mixed/projected schema and matching checkpoint validation; keep current MCC schemas, outputs and numerical paths unchanged. Do not reuse MCC labels to imply an MC pressure state.

Verify weak pressure/volume equations, full assembled nonsymmetric Jacobian, force/constraint residuals, pressure nullspaces, support completeness and exact rollback/recovery on small3D elastic and plastic problems before a large slope solve.

Compare the same original fresh-history slope replay, same physical geometry/material/loading/boundary/requiredfactor and unchanged 2D5percent gates in a separate recorded discretization study. Do not substitute the accepted-origin epoch route.

Distinguish locally admissible constitutive GP stresses from stresses used in mixed equilibrium. Weak pressure consistency alone is not a pointwise admissible equilibrium certificate; SRM lower-side acceptance needs separately validated physical stress/yield/force evidence.
Run old and new complete regressions, actual CLI and independent all-GP checks; only then consider production adoption and an independently verified same-case slope comparison.
